title: The egg valuable that cracks and gets up
summary: One of R.E.P.O.'s trap valuables is an egg: it keeps a time before it goes off, a rest after cracking, arms and legs with a range each, its own light, a crack a scream and an explosion, and it shakes the camera when it goes.
body: This one looks like something to carry and is not. It is a trap before it is a valuable: the game keeps whether the trap has been triggered, whether it is active, whether it has started, whether it works on a timer, and the rarity level it activates at.
It has a fuse of its own. There is a length of time before it goes off and a rest time after it cracks, so the egg has a beginning and a pause rather than a single instant.
It does not sit quietly either. Its jolts come on a range of intervals rather than a fixed rhythm, and it torques itself as it goes, so the egg is already moving before anything else happens.
When it goes off it shakes the camera. The shake has a length, a strength and bounds of its own, which is how the game makes the bang felt without moving the room.

It also grows limbs. There is a range for the arms and a range for the legs, with a separate left and right arm and a separate left and right leg, so the egg can put out four limbs rather than being a shell that only splits.
It has its own light and its own mesh to draw, and it breaks in a particle effect kept for that moment, so the light and the break are not borrowed from anything else in the level.
It sounds like exactly what it is. There is a sound for cracking, a scream and an explosion, kept apart from each other.

It knows whether it is the copy that matters locally, and monsters can be set to come and investigate it, so an egg left on the floor is a problem for the people who find it rather than only for the crew carrying it.
The image beside this entry is the game's own: one of the egg textures it ships, a decorated shell with a face painted on it.
What this entry does not tell you: how long the fuse is, how much the explosion hurts, or what the egg is worth. We have not verified those numbers, so we do not print them.
